sections.title: Integration services
sections.subtitle: Connect applications and data so enterprise processes work end to end.

backgroundImage.alt: Connected enterprise application and data integration

sections.heading: Make critical systems work together
sections.body:
Disconnected ERP, CRM, cloud and legacy systems create rekeying, reconciliation work and unclear ownership when exchanges fail. We assess the landscape, design dependable contracts and make integration ownership explicit.

Baseline manual rekeying effort, reconciliation exceptions and operational failures, then agree service objectives for each critical flow. [Discuss your integration priorities](#get-in-touch).

sections.heading: What we deliver
sections.description: One integration scope, from architecture and contracts to reconciliation and operating ownership.

items.title: Integration assessment and architecture
items.description: System and data-owner inventory, dependency map and agreed API, event or batch patterns.

items.title: API design and governance
items.description: Versioned interface contracts, authentication, access rules and change-control responsibilities.

items.title: Boomi and iPaaS implementation
items.description: Configured integrations and deployment procedures for the agreed platform scope. Boomi is a platform we work with, not Linkfields-owned IP.

items.title: Mapping and reconciliation
items.description: Source-to-target mappings, validation rules and reconciliation checks, with retries and failure queues.

items.title: Managed integration and observability
items.description: Alerts, transaction tracing, operating runbooks and named support ownership against agreed service objectives.

sections.heading: One connected enterprise process
sections.description: Illustrative CRM order → ERP fulfilment → finance reconciliation flow. Define the contracts and accountable owners at each handover.

items.title: 1. Capture and validate the order
items.description: CRM sends a versioned API request with agreed access and validation rules. The integration owner manages transformations and routes rejected records to a failure queue.

items.title: 2. Fulfil and handle exceptions
items.description: ERP returns fulfilment status through an agreed interface. Trace retries and duplicate requests; route business exceptions to an owner rather than silently retrying.

items.title: 3. Reconcile and operate
items.description: Finance checks completeness and values against source records. Operations monitors failures, with cloud access, rollback and runbooks agreed before deployment.

sections.heading: Integration IP with clear boundaries
sections.description: Choose reusable delivery IP and product capabilities against the target architecture; do not assume an unspecified connector library.

items.title: Modernisation & Integration Toolkit
items.description: Reusable delivery IP for modernisation and integration. Agree what can be reused and what requires client-specific contracts, mappings and engineering.

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: REST APIs and composable applications can address custom integration and business capabilities where ERP or CRM does not fit; this is distinct from Boomi.

items.title: testoriumz
items.description: Continuous testing and CI/CD integration support end-to-end regression, alongside Automated Testing & Release Assurance Packs and Cyber-Safe Delivery.

sections.note: Products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without a Linkfields services engagement. Discovery agrees product fit, reusable accelerator content and client-specific engineering.

sections.heading: From integration landscape to dependable operations

items.description: Inventory — Identify systems, interfaces, data owners and failure patterns. Client owners confirm access, critical transactions and the reconciliation baseline.
Design — Agree contracts, target patterns, access controls and transformations. Obtain sign-off from system, data and security owners before building the selected integrations.
Build and validate — Implement mappings and connections; test end-to-end flows, reconciliation and security. Demonstrate retry, duplicate and failure handling against acceptance criteria.
Deploy and operate — Validate cutover and rollback, transfer runbooks and alert ownership, then monitor and improve. Record platform versions, change responsibilities and agreed service objectives.

sections.heading: Evidence of dependable exchange
sections.body:
Acceptance includes approved API contracts, source-to-target mappings, reconciliation results and tests of failed or duplicate transactions. System owners review access and versioning; operations accepts alerts, runbooks and rollback procedures.

Compare manual effort, reconciliation exceptions and operational failures with the agreed baseline. Record transaction scope and measurement period so changes in reliability can be interpreted correctly.

See [Our approach and commercial models](/company/our-approach) for delivery governance and engagement details.

sections.heading: Plan the right engagement
sections.description: Use Time & Materials for landscape discovery, or Fixed Price for well-defined integration flows. A Dedicated Team supports an evolving integration estate; Managed Service covers agreed monitoring and support. Outcome-Based terms require reliable baselines, service ownership and attribution.

items.title: Which systems and contracts need assessment?
items.description: Identify source and target systems, interface and platform versions, data owners, volumes, critical flows and authentication. Existing contracts and current failure records help define the scope.

items.title: How is reconciliation designed?
items.description: Agree completeness, value and timing checks with business and data owners. Record rejected, missing or duplicated transactions and the process for investigating differences.

items.title: What happens when an integration fails?
items.description: Define retries, failure queues, alerts and escalation for each flow. A named owner should be able to trace the transaction, resolve its cause and replay it safely where appropriate.

items.title: Who owns integrations after delivery?
items.description: Agree ownership of APIs, platform configuration, mappings and source-system changes. A managed scope can cover monitoring and support, with service objectives and exclusions explicitly contracted.

items.title: What should we bring to the conversation?
items.description: Share source and target systems, data flows and current integration failures. We can then agree discovery scope, access and confidentiality requirements.
